moods/imperative/request-k-entreaty-poli.formation: An imperative used as a request rather than a demand, typically from someone of lower rank to a superior, or in a plea: 'please…', 'give me…'. The context, a verb of asking or a pleading tone shows that it is a request; it is usually aorist.

moods/imperative/permissive-imperative-i.description: used in response to an act being done or already done; permission, allowance, or toleration

moods/imperative/conditional-imperative.description: state a condition (protasis) on which the fulfillment (apodosis) of another verb depends; almost always imperative + καί+ future indicative; imperative is is still “commanding”
moods/imperative/conditional-imperative.formation: An imperative followed by καί and a future indicative, the imperative stating the condition on which the future depends: 'work, and you will eat' means 'if you work (and you should), you will eat'. The imperative keeps its force as a command.

moods/imperative/potential-imperative-de.description: imperative in apodosis of implied condition with a conditional imperative in protasis

moods/imperative/pronouncement-imperativ.description: imperative in the passive voice equivalent of a statement that is fulfilled at the moment of speaking

moods/imperative/as-stereotyped-greeting.description: injunctive force suppressed; used for exclamation (e.g., χαῖρε [Greetings!])

tense.description: indicates the speaker’s presentation of the verbal action [or state] with reference to its aspect and, under certain conditions, its time

tense/present.description: Portrays the action as an internal or progressive event, without regard for beginning or end; in indicative, present time (generally)

tense/present/instantaneous-present-k-ao.display_name: Instantaneous Present (a.k.a. Aoristic or Punctiliar Present)
tense/present/instantaneous-present-k-ao.description: action occurs at the moment of speaking; usually a performative statement (e.g., “I tell you the truth, the Rams won the game”); indicative only
tense/present/instantaneous-present-k-ao.formation: A present indicative, usually first person, of a verb of declaring, requesting or granting, whose action is complete in the uttering of it: saying the words is doing the thing ('I promise', 'I name you my heir', 'you are released'). The progressive sense drops out. It occurs only in the indicative, most often in direct speech.

tense/present/progressive-present-k-desc.description: at this present time, right now (describes a scene in progress, esp. in narrative literature)
tense/present/progressive-present-k-desc.formation: A present tense describing an action going on at the moment of speaking, 'right now': a scene in progress rather than a habit or a general truth. The action is continuous rather than repeated. It is common in direct speech within narrative, in the indicative and the other moods.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/extend.description: describes an action which, begun in the past, continues in the present; translate like an English present perfect
tense/present/broad-band-presents/extend.formation: A present indicative for an action begun in the past and still going on, rendered with an English perfect: 'I have worked this field for twenty years'. A time expression reaching back (so many years, a long time, from the beginning) normally marks it, and the emphasis falls on the present.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/iterat.description: repeatedly, continuously (describes an event that repeatedly happens [indicative if in present time]); includes distributive present (individual acts distributed to more than one object)
tense/present/broad-band-presents/iterat.formation: A present tense for an action that happens again and again at short, irregular intervals: 'keeps on', 'repeatedly'. An adverb of frequency often marks it (often, always, without ceasing), and it is frequent in present imperatives. It includes the distributive present, one act repeated across many people.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/custom.description: signals either an action that regularly occurs or an ongoing state (broader, more regular than iterative)
tense/present/broad-band-presents/custom.formation: A present tense for an action that recurs regularly, as a habit or practice, or for an ongoing state: 'customarily', 'habitually'. It is broader and more regular than the iterative, and is often marked by a phrase of regular frequency (twice a week, every year, as is the custom).

tense/present/broad-band-presents/gnomic.description: does happen (rather than is happening); states a general, timeless fact, often proverbial in character
tense/present/broad-band-presents/gnomic.formation: A present tense stating a general, timeless truth, something that does happen rather than is happening: the way of nature or of people in general. It usually has a generic subject or object (every tree, no one, a person), often in a proverb or maxim.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: describes a past event in narrative literature (only indicative, third person; used for vividness; λέγει most common; εἰμί does not occur; aspectually equivalent of aorist)
tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.formation: A present indicative used in narrative for a past event, set among aorists and imperfects. It is third person only, most often a verb of saying or coming, and never εἰμί. English renders it as a simple past; it marks a new scene, a new participant or a turn in the story.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: used to emphasize that the results of a past action are still continuing (lexical type [e.g., ἥκω] and contextual type [to introduce OT quotations])
tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.formation: A present indicative whose action lies in the past but whose result still stands, rendered with an English perfect: 'he has come', 'they have received it in full'. It is chiefly lexical, with verbs such as ἥκω, ἀπέχω and ἀκούω ('I hear that…'); it also introduces a written saying that still speaks.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: portrays subject as desiring to do something (voluntative), attempting to do something (conative), or at the point of almost doing something (tendential)

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.display_name: In Progress, but Not Complete (True Conative)
tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: is attempting (unsuccessfully) (attempt is being made in the present time [indicative mood])

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.display_name: Not Begun, but About/Desired to be Attempted (Voluntative/Tendential)
tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: about to (an attempt is about to be made or is desired to be made in the present time [or, very near future time])

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.formation: A present indicative for an action attempted, intended or on the point of happening, but not accomplished: 'is trying to', 'is about to'. The context shows that the action is not, or not yet, carried out; unlike the futuristic present, it carries no certainty.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: describes a future event, typically adding the connotations of immediacy and certainty (usually with verbs whose lexical nuance includes anticipation)
is soon going to, is certainly going to, will
describes an event begun in the present time, but completed in the future (such as is coming, is going)

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.formation: A present indicative for an event still to come, spoken of as though already under way, which adds immediacy or certainty: 'is coming', 'is going to'. It is used mostly with verbs of motion or anticipation (ἔρχομαι, πορεύομαι, compounds of -βαίνω), with a time word or the context pointing ahead.

tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.description: after verb of perception; tense retained from the direct discourse when the saying is put in indirect discourse; translate as though imperfect when main verb is past tense (“they heard that he was at home”)
tense/present/broad-band-presents/specia.formation: A present tense inside indirect discourse after a past verb of perceiving, knowing, thinking or hearing (often with ὅτι), keeping the tense of the original words; English shifts it back to a past: 'they heard that he was ill'. It is a matter of translation more than a separate use.

tense/imperfect.description: Portrays the action as an internal or progressive event (“motion picture”), without regard for beginning or end; occurs only in indicative, past time (generally)

tense/imperfect/instantaneous-imperfect-.display_name: Instantaneous Imperfect (a.k.a. Aoristic or Punctiliar Imperfect)
tense/imperfect/instantaneous-imperfect-.description: in narrative, ἔλεγεν is sometimes equivalent to an aorist (= “he said”)

tense/imperfect/progressive-descriptive-.description: was (continually) doing, was (right then) happening (in progress in past time)
tense/imperfect/progressive-descriptive-.formation: An imperfect describing an action or state in progress at a point in past time, 'was doing': often the background against which another event happens, or a scene painted as it unfolds.

tense/imperfect/ingressive-inchoative-in.description: began doing (stresses the beginning of an action, with the implications that it continued for some time; frequent in narrative to note a topic shift)
tense/imperfect/ingressive-inchoative-in.formation: An imperfect stressing the start of an action that then went on, 'began doing'. It is common in narrative where a new activity or topic begins, often right after an aorist that sets it off.

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/it.description: kept on, repeatedly (repeated action in past time)
tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/it.formation: An imperfect for an action repeated in past time over a limited span, 'kept on doing': by one person again and again, or by many people each in turn (distributive). A phrase such as 'day by day' or 'one by one' often marks it.

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/cu.description: customarily or habitually (habitual), continually (general); indicates a regularly recurring activity in past time (habitual) or a state that continued for some time (general)
tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/cu.formation: An imperfect for an action that recurred regularly in past time, as a habit, or for a state that lasted: 'used to', 'was accustomed to'. A phrase of regular frequency (every year, daily, at each festival) often marks it.

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.description: indicates time antecedent to that of the main verb (which also indicates past time)
portrays the action as something that was desired (voluntative), attempted (conative), or at the point of almost doing something (tendential)

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.display_name: In Progress, but Not Complete (True Conative)
tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.description: was attempting (unsuccessfully) (attempt made in past time)

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.display_name: Not Begun, but About/Desired to be Attempted (Voluntative/Tendential)
tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.description: was about to, could almost wish (an attempt was about to be made or one that was almost desired to be made)

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.formation: An imperfect for an action attempted, wanted or on the point of being done in the past but not carried through: 'was trying to', 'was about to'. With verbs of wishing it gives a polite or unfulfilled wish, 'I would like', 'I could wish'. The context shows that the action did not come about.

tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.description: after a verb of perception; tense retained from the direct discourse when the saying is put in indirect discourse; translate as though pluperfect (“the Jews did not believe that he had been blind [ὅτι ἦν τυφλός]”)
tense/imperfect/broad-band-imperfects/sp.formation: An imperfect inside indirect discourse after a past verb of perceiving, knowing, believing or remembering, keeping the tense of the original thought; English shifts it back to a pluperfect: 'she did not believe that he had been away'.

tense/aorist.description: Presents action as a whole; summary tense; takes a snapshot of the action; past time in the indicative

tense/aorist/constative-complexive-punct.description: views the action as a whole, taking no interest in its internal workings; describes the action in summary fashion
tense/aorist/constative-complexive-punct.formation: An aorist presenting an action as a whole, as a simple fact, with no interest in its beginning, progress or end. The action may have been momentary, repeated a number of times, or long, lasting for years; the aorist says only that it happened. It is the aorist's ordinary use and the backbone of narrative.

tense/aorist/ingressive-inceptive-inchoa.description: began to do, became (stresses the beginning of an action, or the entrance into a state)
tense/aorist/ingressive-inceptive-inchoa.formation: An aorist stressing entry into a state or the start of an action: 'became', 'began to'. It is usual with verbs of state (be angry, be poor, be rich, be well), where the aorist marks the change into the state; unlike the ingressive imperfect, it says nothing about the action continuing.

tense/aorist/consummative-culminative-ec.description: stresses the cessation of an act or state
tense/aorist/consummative-culminative-ec.formation: An aorist stressing the end or accomplishment of an action or effort, often rendered with an English perfect: 'has arrived', 'has learned'. It is common with verbs that name an outcome (arrive, die, persuade, learn), or where the context shows a process brought to its conclusion.

tense/aorist/gnomic-aorist.description: presents a timeless, general (generic) fact; translate like simple present tense

tense/aorist/epistolary-aorist.description: aorist indicative in the epistles in which the author self-consciously describes his letter from the time frame of the audience
tense/aorist/epistolary-aorist.formation: An aorist indicative in a letter by which the writer describes his own writing or sending from the time of the readers, for whom it will be past: 'I have sent him to you' of the one carrying the letter, 'I have written' of the letter in hand. It is used chiefly with verbs of sending and writing.

tense/aorist/proleptic-futuristic-aorist.description: describes an event that is not yet past as though it were already completed
tense/aorist/proleptic-futuristic-aorist.formation: An aorist indicative for an event that has not yet happened, spoken of as already done to stress its certainty, often in the result of a condition: 'if the ship holds, we are saved'. The context makes plain that the event is still future.

tense/aorist/immediate-past-aorist-drama.description: just now (describes an event that happened rather recently or at the present moment)
tense/aorist/immediate-past-aorist-drama.formation: An aorist indicative for something that has just happened or has just now come about, 'has just', often with ἄρτι or νῦν; with verbs of knowing and feeling the new state is present, as in 'I've got it!' of an idea that has just come.

tense/future.description: External portrayal (like aorist) in future (subsequent) time

tense/future/predictive-future.description: indicates that something will take place or come to pass
tense/future/predictive-future.formation: A future indicative stating that something will take place: the ordinary use of the tense, often with a phrase of future time (in those days, on that day).

tense/future/imperatival-future.description: used for a command, almost always in OT quotations
tense/future/imperatival-future.formation: A future indicative, usually second person, used as a command, or with οὐ as a prohibition: 'you shall pay the worker', 'you shall not take it'. It is categorical or solemn rather than a milder imperative, and usually has a universal or legal ring.

tense/future/deliberative-future.description: asks a question that implies some doubt about the response—one of possibility, desirability, or necessity
tense/future/deliberative-future.formation: A future indicative in a question, usually first person, asking what one should or can do: 'what shall we do?', 'where shall we go?', 'should we sell the field?' The question implies doubt about the answer, or is a real appeal for advice; the aorist subjunctive does the same work more often.

tense/future/gnomic-future.description: indicates the likelihood that a (true to life) generic event will take place

tense/future/miscellaneous-subjunctive-e.description: sometimes used in situations normally reserved for the aorist subjunctive

tense/perfect.description: Describes an event which, completed in the past (we are speaking of the perfect indicative), has results existing in the present time; combines aorist and present

tense/perfect/intensive-perfect-k-result.description: emphasizes the results or present state produced by a past action (often best translated like English present); frequent with stative verbs
tense/perfect/intensive-perfect-k-result.formation: A perfect stressing the present state produced by a past action, usually best rendered as an English present: 'the gate is shut', 'now they know'. It is frequent with verbs of state.

tense/perfect/extensive-perfect-k-consum.description: emphasizes the completed action of a past action from which a present state emerges (best translated like English present perfect); frequent with transitive verbs
tense/perfect/extensive-perfect-k-consum.formation: A perfect stressing the completed action from which a present state follows, rendered with an English present perfect: 'I have finished the work', 'the builders have raised the wall'. It is frequent with transitive verbs.

tense/perfect/aoristic-perfect-k-dramati.display_name: Aoristic Perfect (a.k.a. Dramatic or Historical Perfect)
tense/perfect/aoristic-perfect-k-dramati.description: rhetorical use of the perfect as a simple past without concern for results; in narrative literature, contextually conditioned
tense/perfect/aoristic-perfect-k-dramati.formation: A perfect indicative used in narrative as a simple past, set among aorists, with no interest in any lasting result: 'he came and took it'. It lends vividness or climax to one act in a sequence.

tense/perfect/perfect-present-force.description: focus on present state in which the completed action is not in view; lexically conditioned (e.g., οἶδα, ἕστηκα)
tense/perfect/perfect-present-force.formation: A perfect of a few verbs (οἶδα, ἵστημι, παρίστημι, πείθω) used simply as a present, with no past act in view: 'I know', 'he stands', 'I am convinced'. The result of the action has become the action itself.

tense/perfect/gnomic-perfect.description: speaks of a generic or proverbial occurrence; normal aspect, but distributive subjects/actions

tense/perfect/proleptic-futuristic-perfe.description: refers to a state resulting from an antecedent action that is future from the time of speaking

tense/perfect/perfect-allegory.description: OT event is viewed in terms of its allegorical or applicational value (Melchizedek “has received tithes [δεδεκάτωκεν] from Abraham”)

tense/pluperfect.description: Existing results in the past (it occurs only in the indicative); combines aorist and imperfect

tense/pluperfect/intensive-pluperfect-re.description: emphasizes resultant state that existed in past time (translate as simple past)
tense/pluperfect/intensive-pluperfect-re.formation: A pluperfect stressing a state that existed in past time as the result of an earlier action, rendered as a simple past: 'it was already dark', 'the house was built of stone'. It often sets the scene for the main events.

tense/pluperfect/extensive-pluperfect-co.description: emphasize the completion of an action in past time (had + perfect passive participle)
tense/pluperfect/extensive-pluperfect-co.formation: A pluperfect stressing an action completed before another past event, rendered 'had done': 'the others had already left'. It supplies background that lies before the main line of the narrative.

tense/pluperfect/pluperfect-simple-past-.display_name: Pluperfect with a Simple Past Force
tense/pluperfect/pluperfect-simple-past-.description: focus on past state in which the completed action is not in view; lexically conditioned (e.g., ᾔδειν, εἱστήκειν)
tense/pluperfect/pluperfect-simple-past-.formation: A pluperfect of a few stative verbs (οἶδα, ἵστημι, παρίστημι, εἴωθα) used simply as a past, with no earlier act in view: 'he knew', 'they were standing', 'as he was accustomed'.

infinitive/adverbial/purpose.description: to, in order to, for the purpose of (indicates the purpose or goal of the action or state of its controlling verb)
infinitive/adverbial/purpose.formation: An infinitive stating the aim of its controlling verb: 'went to prepare', 'put on armour so as to be able'. It may follow the verb bare, especially a verb of motion, or be introduced by τοῦ, εἰς τό, πρὸς τό or ὡς. Its subject, when it differs from the main verb's, is in the accusative.

infinitive/adverbial/result.description: so that, so as to, with the result that (indicates the outcome produced by the controlling verb; emphasis on effect, whether intended or not)
infinitive/adverbial/result.formation: An infinitive stating the outcome of its controlling verb, whether intended or not: 'so that', 'with the result that'. It is usually introduced by ὥστε, less often by εἰς τό or ὡς, and its subject, when expressed, is in the accusative. Purpose looks to the aim, result to the effect.

infinitive/adverbial/time/antecedent.description: μετὰ τό + infinitive; translate after + appropriate finite verb

infinitive/adverbial/time/contemporaneou.description: ἐν τῷ + infinitive; translate while, as, when + appropriate finite verb

infinitive/adverbial/time/subsequent.description: πρὸ τοῦ, πρίν, or πρὶν ἤ + infinitive; translate before + appropriate finite verb

infinitive/adverbial/time.formation: An articular infinitive after a preposition, setting the time of its controlling verb: μετὰ τό 'after' (the infinitive's action comes first), ἐν τῷ 'while', 'as' (at the same time), πρὸ τοῦ or πρίν (ἤ) 'before' (it comes later). Its subject is in the accusative, and English renders it with a finite clause.

infinitive/adverbial/cause.description: διὰ τό + infinitive; indicates the reason for the action of the controlling verb; translate because + appropriate finite verb
infinitive/adverbial/cause.formation: διὰ τό with an infinitive, giving the reason for the action of its controlling verb: 'because'. The infinitive's subject, when expressed, is in the accusative, and English renders it with a finite verb: 'because it had no root'.

infinitive/adverbial/means.description: ἐν τῷ + infinitive; describes the way in which the action of the controlling verb is accomplished; translate by … doing, etc.

infinitive/adverbial/complementary-suppl.description: used with a “helper” verb (the most common are ἄρχομαι, βούλομαι, δύναμαι, ἐπιτρέπω, ζητέω, θέλω, μέλλω, ὀφείλω) to complete its thought
infinitive/adverbial/complementary-suppl.formation: An infinitive completing a helper verb that is incomplete without it: 'is able to', 'want you to', 'begin to', 'is about to', 'ought to'. The usual helpers are δύναμαι, θέλω, βούλομαι, ἄρχομαι, μέλλω, ὀφείλω, ζητέω and ἐπιτρέπω. The infinitive normally shares the helper's subject; after θέλω or βούλομαι a different subject stands in the accusative.

infinitive/substantival/subject.description: functions as subject of verb, especially with impersonal verbs such as δεῖ, ἔξεστιν
infinitive/substantival/subject.formation: An infinitive or infinitive phrase serving as the subject of a verb: of εἰμί with a predicate ('to die is gain', 'it is not good to take…'), or of an impersonal verb such as δεῖ, ἔξεστιν or συμφέρει. It may carry the article τό or stand without it.

infinitive/substantival/direct-object.description: occurring after other than a verb of perception or communication
infinitive/substantival/direct-object.formation: An infinitive serving as the direct object of a verb that is not a verb of saying or perceiving: 'finish the doing', 'you revived your concern'. It often carries the article (τό, or τοῦ after a verb taking the genitive), which marks it as the thing done. With a helper verb and no article it is complementary instead.

infinitive/substantival/indirect-discour.description: specialized direct object after a verb of perception or communication; represents a finite verb of direct discourse (“I told you to do the dishes” in the direct discourse would have been, “Do the dishes”); retains the tense of the direct discourse and usually represents either an imperative or indicative
infinitive/substantival/indirect-discour.formation: An infinitive after a verb of saying, thinking, asking or perceiving, reporting what was said, believed or requested: 'they say there is no…', 'they asked him to stay'. It stands for the finite verb of the direct form and keeps that verb's tense. Its subject, when it differs from the main verb's, is in the accusative.

infinitive/substantival/appositional.description: namely; stands in apposition to a noun, pronoun, or substantival adjective (or some other substantive); defines the substantive
infinitive/substantival/appositional.formation: An infinitive in apposition to a noun, pronoun or substantival adjective, stating what it consists of: 'namely, to…'. A demonstrative (τοῦτο, αὕτη) often points forward to it. It defines the word it stands beside and could replace it, where an epexegetical infinitive only explains it.

infinitive/substantival/epexegetical.description: clarifies, explains, or qualifies a noun or adjective (words that indicate ability, authority, desire, freedom, hope, need, obligation, or readiness)
infinitive/substantival/epexegetical.formation: An infinitive completing a noun or adjective of ability, authority, desire, freedom, need, readiness or worth: 'quick to hear', 'authority to tread', 'worthy to be called'. It says in what respect the word applies; it may be bare or take τοῦ or εἰς τό. Unlike an appositional infinitive, it cannot replace the word.

infinitive/independent/imperatival.description: functions just like an imperative; not dependent on any other verb (do not confuse with indirect discourse infinitive)

infinitive/independent/absolute.description: bears no syntactical relation to anything else in the sentence; (e.g., χαίρειν = Greetings!)

structural-categories/without-governing-.description: Only 2 Cor 2:13: either causal or contemporaneous time

participle/adjectival-participles.description: adjectival nature is emphasized over verbal; if the participle is articular, it must be adjectival; if anarthrous, it may be adjectival

participle/adjectival-proper-dependent/a.description: who, which; functions like an attributive adjective, in any standard attributive position

participle/adjectival-proper-dependent/p.description: functions like a predicate adjective in predicate position (though usually in predicate position, the participle is adverbial)

participle/adjectival-proper-dependent.formation: A participle modifying a noun like an adjective, agreeing with it in gender, number and case. Attributive, it stands in an attributive position (usually article–noun–article–participle, or article–participle–noun) and is best rendered as a relative clause, 'the — who/which …'. Predicate, it has no article and asserts something of the noun, often a perfect passive ('found … opened').

participle/substantival-independent.description: the one who, the thing which; functions in the place of a substantive; can perform virtually any function a noun can; verbal aspect usually retained
participle/substantival-independent.formation: A participle standing in place of a noun, usually with the article: 'the one who —', 'those who —', 'the thing that —'. Its case follows its role in the sentence (subject, object, indirect object, object of a preposition), and it keeps its verbal side, taking its own object and modifiers.

participle/verbal-participles.description: verbal nature is emphasized over adjectival; only with anarthrous participles, usually nominative and dependent on main verb

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: modifies the verb, answering the question When? (temporal), How? (means, manner), Why? (purpose, cause), etc.
answers the question When? May be antecedent (after doing, after he did), contemporaneous (while doing), or subsequent (before doing, before he does)
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle giving the time of the main verb's action: 'after —ing', 'when', 'while'. An aorist participle before the verb is usually antecedent ('after he did'); a present participle is usually contemporaneous ('while doing'). The time is relative to the main verb, not to the speaker.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: answers the question, How? by + participle of emotion or attitude (easily confused with means)
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle telling how the main action was done in the sense of the emotion or attitude that went with it: 'he went away grieving', 'they went on rejoicing'. It adds colour; unlike a participle of means, removing it would not remove the point of the main verb.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: by means of (answering the question, How?); indicates the means by which the action of a finite verb is accomplished; defines or explains the controlling verb; usually follows the verb
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle giving the means by which the main action is accomplished: 'by —ing'. It usually follows a vaguer or more general main verb and defines it, and it is normally contemporaneous with it, usually present tense.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: because (answers the question, Why?); indicates the cause or reason or ground of the action of the finite verb; usually precedes its verb
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle giving the reason or ground for the main action: 'because', 'since'. It normally precedes the main verb, and is often aorist or perfect (an adverbial perfect participle is almost always causal), though present participles serve too.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: if (implies a condition on which the fulfillment of the idea indicated by the main verb depends)
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle stating a condition on which the main action depends: 'if'. It usually stands for a third class condition, something uncertain or hypothetical, and the main verb is often future or a general statement.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: although (implies that the state or action of the main verb is true in spite of the state or action of the participle)
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle stating something in spite of which the main action holds: 'although', 'even though'. It is built like a causal participle, usually preceding the verb, but the relation is the reverse; καίπερ or καίτοι sometimes make the concession explicit.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: translate like an infinitive or with the purpose of (indicates the purpose/intent of the action of the finite verb); usually follows main verb
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle giving the purpose of the main action, best rendered like an English infinitive: 'to —', 'in order to —'. It follows the main verb and is future or present (rarely aorist), often a verb that itself implies aim, such as seeking or testing.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: with the result of (indicates the actual outcome or result of the action of the main verb); can be internal (logical) or external (temporal); follows main verb
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An adverbial participle giving the actual outcome of the main action, intended or not: 'with the result that', 'thus —ing'. It is present tense and follows the main verb; the result may be the logical implication of the action or what came of it afterward.

An anarthrous participle subordinate to a finite verb, telling the circumstances of its action: when, how, by what means, why, under what condition, in spite of what. It agrees with the verb's subject (or with the noun it describes), and the relation to the verb is not marked by the form but read from the context, the tense and the word order.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: translate as finite verb + and (it describes an action that, in some sense, is coordinate with the finite verb; “piggy-backs” on mood of main verb); five structural clues usually found:
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: A participle describing an action coordinate with the main verb and taking on its mood, rendered as a second finite verb joined by 'and': 'get up and go', 'they left everything and followed'. Usually an aorist participle before an aorist imperative or indicative, in narrative; the participle is the preliminary step, the main verb the point.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: anarthrous participle in the accusative case, in conjunction with an accusative noun or pronoun, sometimes indicates indirect discourse after a verb of perception or communication; retains tense of direct discourse
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An anarthrous participle, with a noun or pronoun in the same case, after a verb of perceiving or saying, giving the content of what is heard, seen, known or reported: 'he heard that there was grain'. The participle keeps the tense of the direct statement.

participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.description: completes the thought of another verb; e.g., “I do not cease praying for you”
anarthrous participle used with a verb of being to form a finite verbal idea; see table below for various combinations (647–49):
participle/verbal-participles/dependent-.formation: An anarthrous participle with a form of εἰμί (sometimes γίνομαι or ὑπάρχω) making a single verbal idea: imperfect of εἰμί with a present participle for a progressive past ('was teaching'), present of εἰμί with a perfect participle for a perfect ('are numbered'), imperfect with a perfect participle for a pluperfect, future with a present participle for a progressive future.

participle/pluperfect/redundant-pleonast.description: verb of saying (or thinking) used with a participle with basically the same meaning (as in ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν)
participle/pluperfect/redundant-pleonast.formation: A participle of saying or thinking used alongside a finite verb of much the same meaning, as in 'answering, he said' or 'he spoke, saying'. The pair describes a single act, and English usually renders just one verb ('he replied'). It is almost wholly a feature of the Gospel narratives.

participle/pluperfect/as-imperative-impe.description: functions just like an imperative; participle not to be attached to any verb in the context, grammatically independent

participle/pluperfect/as-indicative-inde.display_name: As an Indicative (Independent Proper or Absolute)
participle/pluperfect/as-indicative-inde.description: functions like declarative indicative; participle stands alone in a declarative sense as the only verb in a clause or sentence
substantival participle that fits the case description of nominativus pendens—logical rather than syntactical subject at beginning of a sentence
anarthrous genitive participle with genitive substantive, functioning adverbially (usually temporal), but grammatically independent of verb in main clause

clauses-general/independent-clauses.description: a clause that is not subordinate to another clause

clauses-general/dependent-clauses.description: a clause that is subordinate to another clause

clauses-general/dependent-clauses/struct.display_name: Structure (not all occur with every syntactical function) (659–60)

clauses-general/dependent-clauses/syntac.description: can function as a subject, predicate nominative, direct object, indirect discourse, apposition
attributive function only; describes, explains, or restricts a substantive
modifies a verb as follows: cause, comparison, concession, condition, complementary, location, manner/means, purpose, result, time

conjunctions/logical-functions.description: relate the movement of thought from one passage to another by expressing logical relationships

conjunctions/ascensive.description: even (final addition or point of focus); καί, δέ, and μηδέ
conjunctions/ascensive.formation: καί (also δέ, or μηδέ in the negative) adding a final item that goes beyond what came before, often the most surprising or extreme: 'even'. The added item is the point of focus, the top of a rising series.

conjunctions/connective-continuative-coo.description: and, also (if emphatic [adjunctive]); (connects an additional element to a discussion); καί and δέ
conjunctions/connective-continuative-coo.formation: καί or δέ simply joining a further element to what precedes, word to word, clause to clause or sentence to sentence: 'and', or with emphasis 'also'. δέ is often best left untranslated; καί carries the main line of a narrative forward.

conjunctions/contrastive-adversative.description: but, rather, however (contrast or opposing thought to the idea to which it is connected); ἀλλά, πλήν, sometimes καί and δέ
conjunctions/contrastive-adversative.formation: A conjunction setting what follows against what precedes: 'but', 'rather', 'however'. ἀλλά is the strong contrast, typically after a negative ('not this, but that'); δέ is milder; πλήν means 'but', 'nevertheless'; καί can also carry contrast when the context demands it.

conjunctions/correlative.description: paired conjunctions expressing various relationships; e.g., μέν … δέ (on the one hand … on the other hand); καί … καί (both … and)
conjunctions/correlative.formation: Paired conjunctions that set two members in a fixed relation: μέν … δέ ('on the one hand … on the other'), καί … καί ('both … and'), οὔτε … οὔτε ('neither … nor'), εἴτε … εἴτε ('whether … or'), ἤ … ἤ ('either … or'). The first word announces the second, and the two members are balanced against each other.

conjunctions/disjunctive-alternative.description: or (suggests an alternative possibility to the idea to which it is connected); ἤ
conjunctions/disjunctive-alternative.formation: ἤ presenting an alternative to what precedes: 'or'. The alternatives may be opposites or related options, between words, phrases or clauses; repeated, it gives 'either … or'.

conjunctions/emphatic.description: certainly, indeed (involves intensifying the normal sense of a conjunction); ἀλλά (certainly), οὐ μή (certainly not or by no means), οὖν (certainly); true emphatic conjunctions include γε, δή, μενοῦνγε, μέντοι, ναί, and νή
conjunctions/emphatic.formation: A particle or conjunction that intensifies the word or clause it stands with: 'indeed', 'certainly'. The true emphatic particles are γε, δή, μενοῦνγε, μέντοι, ναί and νή; ἀλλά and οὖν can also be emphatic in context. γε and δή are postpositive and highlight the word just before them.

conjunctions/explanatory.description: for, you see, or that is, namely (conjunction indicates additional information being given to what has been described); γάρ, δέ, εἰ (after verbs of emotion), and καί
conjunctions/explanatory.formation: A conjunction introducing additional information that explains or clarifies what has just been said: 'for', 'you see', 'that is'. γάρ is the usual word, and δέ can introduce a parenthetical aside; the explanation is background and less prominent than what it explains.

conjunctions/inferential.description: therefore (gives a deduction, conclusion, or summary to the preceding discussion); ἄρα, γάρ, διό, διότι, οὖν, πλήν, τοιγαροῦν, τοινῦν, and ὥστε.
conjunctions/inferential.formation: A conjunction drawing a conclusion, deduction or summary from what precedes: 'therefore', 'so', 'then'. The usual words are οὖν (postpositive), διό, ἄρα and ὥστε with the indicative; the conclusion is the more prominent part.

conjunctions/transitional.description: now, then (involves the change to a new topic of discussion, especially in narrative); οὖν and especially δέ
conjunctions/transitional.formation: A conjunction marking a move in the narrative rather than a logical link: a new scene, a new participant, a change of time, or a return to the main line after an aside: 'now', 'then'. δέ is by far the most common; οὖν does this especially in narrative, where it resumes the story.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions.description: amplify the verbal idea in a specific way (usually subordinate conjunctions)

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/causal.description: because, since (expresses the basis or ground of an action); γάρ, διότι, ἐπεί, ἐπειδή, ἐπειδήπερ, καθώς, ὅτι, and ὡς
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/causal.formation: A conjunction giving the reason or ground for an action or statement: 'because', 'since'. ὅτι, διότι, ἐπεί and ἐπειδή introduce a dependent causal clause with the indicative; γάρ gives the reason in a clause of its own.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/compara.description: as, just as, in the same way, thus, or in this manner (suggests an analogy or comparison between the connected   p 762  ideas or tells how something is to be done); καθάπερ, καθώς, οὕτως, ὡς, ὡσαύτως, ὡσεί, and ὥσπερ
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/compara.formation: A conjunction drawing a comparison or telling how something is done: 'as', 'just as', 'like'. The usual words are ὡς, καθώς, ὥσπερ and καθάπερ, often answered by οὕτως ('so') in the main clause.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/conditi.description: if (introduces a protasis of a conditional clause); εἰ and ἐάν
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/conditi.formation: εἰ or ἐάν introducing the 'if' clause of a condition, on which the main clause depends. εἰ takes the indicative (and rarely the optative); ἐάν takes the subjunctive. εἰ μή and ἐὰν μή mean 'unless', 'except'.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/local-s.description: where, from where, or the place which (gives the location or sphere [metaphorically], that is, the context in which an action takes place); ὅθεν, ὅπου, and οὗ
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/local-s.formation: ὅπου, οὗ or ὅθεν introducing a clause that gives the place, or metaphorically the sphere, of an action: 'where', 'from where'. They take the indicative, or the subjunctive with ἄν or ἐάν for 'wherever'.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/purpose.description: in order that (indicates the goal or aim of an action); ἵνα, ὅπως, μήπως (the negative purpose), μήπου (negative purpose), and μήποτε (negative purpose)
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/purpose.formation: ἵνα or ὅπως with the subjunctive, giving the aim of the main action: 'in order that', 'so that', or simply 'to'. A negative purpose uses ἵνα μή, ὅπως μή or μήποτε: 'so that … not', 'lest'. The main verb usually implies intention.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/result.description: so that, with the result that (gives the outcome or consequence of an action); ὥστε, ὡς, ὅτι, and less frequently, ἵνα
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/result.formation: A conjunction giving the outcome of the main action rather than its aim: 'so that', 'with the result that'. The usual construction is ὥστε with the infinitive (occasionally the indicative); ἵνα with the subjunctive sometimes has this force too.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/tempora.description: translations vary (indicates the time of the action); ἄχρι, ἕως, ὅταν, ὅτε, οὐδέποτε (negative temporal), οὐκέτι (negative temporal), οὔπω (negative temporal), ποτέ, and ὡς
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/tempora.formation: A conjunction placing one action in time relative to another: ὅτε and ὡς 'when', with the indicative; ὅταν 'whenever', with the subjunctive; ἕως, ἄχρι and μέχρι 'until'.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/substan.description: the conjunction introduces a noun content clause and epexegesis

that (conjunction introduces a subject, predicate nominative, direct object, or an appositional noun clause; direct and indirect discourse are specialized object clauses following verbs of expression or perception); ἵνα, ὅπως, ὅτι, and ὡς
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/substan.formation: ὅτι, ἵνα, ὅπως or ὡς introducing a noun clause that serves as subject, object or predicate, or stands in apposition: 'that'. After verbs of saying, knowing or perceiving, ὅτι gives the content of what is said or known; after verbs of asking or urging, ἵνα or ὅπως gives what is asked.

conjunctions/adverbial-functions/substan.description: that (conjunction introducing a clause that completes the idea of a verb, noun, or adjective); ἵνα and ὅτι
conjunctions/adverbial-functions/substan.formation: ἵνα or ὅτι introducing a clause that completes or explains a preceding noun, adjective or verb: 'that', 'to'. It fills out what the word means (worthy to…, need that…, a reward that…), much as an epexegetical infinitive would.

conditional-sentences/conditional-senten.description: there are three common relationships that the protasis can have to the apodosis (regardless of whether the condition is first class, second class, etc.) (682–84):

conditional-sentences/cause-effect.description: protasis indicates the cause of which the apodosis is the result

conditional-sentences/evidence-inference.description: protasis indicates the evidence from which the apodosis supplies the inference

conditional-sentences/equivalence.description: both halves are saying the saying the same thing (“If A, then B” means “A = B”)

conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.display_name: II. Conditional Sentences in Greek (especially the NT)

conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.description: the assumption of truth for the sake of argument (does not mean since, nor is it a simple, logical condition); protasis: εἰ + indicative (in any tense)/apodosis: any mood, any tense (689, 690–94)
conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.formation: εἰ with the indicative, in any tense, in the 'if' clause (negated by οὐ); the 'then' clause may take any mood and tense, often a command or a question. It assumes the condition true for the argument's sake, not that it is true: 'if you have judged me faithful, stay'.

conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.description: the assumption of an untruth (for the sake of argument); protasis: εἰ + indicative of secondary tense (aorist or imperfect usually)/apodosis: ἄν (usually) + secondary tense in indicative (689, 694–96)
conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.formation: εἰ with a past-tense indicative in the 'if' clause (negated by μή), and ἄν with a past-tense indicative in the 'then' clause (ἄν is occasionally omitted). It assumes the condition untrue: with imperfects, 'if I were…, I would be…'; with aorists, 'if they had…, they would have…'.

conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.description: range of nuances: (a) a logical connection (if A, then B) in the present time (present general condition or fifth class condition), (b) hypothetical situation, and (c) more probable future occurrence; ἐάν + subjunctive, any tense; apodosis: any tense, any mood (present indicative for present general condition) (689, 696–99)
conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.formation: ἐάν with the subjunctive, in any tense, in the 'if' clause (negated by μή); the 'then' clause may take any mood and tense, most often a future or present indicative. It projects the condition without asserting it: a general truth ('if anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble'), a likely future, or a mere hypothesis.

conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.description: possible condition in the future, usually remote possibility (such as if he could do something, if perhaps this should occur); protasis: εἰ + optative; apodosis: optative + ἄν (689, 699–701)
conditional-sentences/ii-conditional-sen.formation: εἰ with the optative in the 'if' clause, and ἄν with the optative in the 'then' clause: 'if he should…, he would…', a remote future possibility. The New Testament has no complete example; it has the 'if' clause alone, or with a verbless or indicative 'then' clause, or a 'then' clause (ἄν with the optative) whose condition is left unstated.

volitional-clauses/future-indicative-k-c.display_name: Future Indicative (a.k.a. Cohortative Indicative, Imperatival Future)
volitional-clauses/future-indicative-k-c.formation: A second-person future indicative used as a command, and with οὐ as a prohibition: 'you shall repay…', 'you shall not murder'. It is solemn, universal or timeless, and most often quotes the Old Testament law.

volitional-clauses/aorist-imperative/ing.description: focus on beginning of action, used for urgency especially
focus on beginning of action that will not be completed immediately

volitional-clauses/aorist-imperative/con.description: stress on a solemn, categorical command; “Make this your top priority and do it now!”

volitional-clauses/aorist-imperative.formation: An aorist imperative commands the action as a whole, without regard to its progress: 'consider it all joy', 'go in'. In a specific situation it is often urgent or points to the start of the action; in a general precept it is solemn and categorical: 'do this, and make it your priority'.

volitional-clauses/present-imperative/cu.description: continue; command for action to be continued, action that may or may not have already been going on; general precept, character-building command

volitional-clauses/present-imperative/it.description: repeated action; difficult to distinguish from Customary (shorter intervals, less regular)

volitional-clauses/present-imperative.formation: A present imperative commands the action as a process, from the inside: begin and go on ('work', 'walk'), keep on as a habit ('let him examine himself'), or do it again and again ('let him ask'). It is the normal form for general precepts; in a specific situation it usually means begin and continue.

volitional-clauses/future-indicative-οὐ-.display_name: Future Indicative (+ οὐ or sometimes μή)
volitional-clauses/future-indicative-οὐ-.description: negative command, typically solemn, universal, or timeless (and usually OT quotation)

volitional-clauses/aorist-subjunctive-μή.formation: μή with an aorist subjunctive, the normal second-person prohibition of the aorist (the aorist imperative is not used this way in the second person): 'do not think that…', 'do not withhold…'. It forbids the action as a whole, which often amounts to 'do not start'. A third-person subjunctive is used the same way, rarely: 'let no one despise him'.

volitional-clauses/present-imperative-μή.description: makes no comment about whether prohibited action is already in progress
